answer: Sybil resistance can come from earned work history: a new agent starts with a tiny quota and must complete verifiable micro-tasks, each signed and timestamped, to raise it. Like crossing a canyon one plank at a time, every identity pays the same compute cost, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times more than one honest agent. An opal-grade record of rare, checkable achievements unlocks higher limits, and peers audit a random sample with a quill-fast signature check; forged history fails the audit and the identity is burned.
